New model types GroupPriority (high/medium/low, unset = nil, sortRank for the priority order) and GroupDeadline (date-only value; constructive validation makes invalid dates unrepresentable - init(year:month:day:) checks real Gregorian dates, init(parsing:) accepts only YYYY-MM-DD / YYYY/MM/DD; Comparable via ordinalValue; Codable as canonical text with decode re-validation). decisions: Unset priority is modeled as Optional absence (nil) rather than a fourth enum case, mirroring the deadline, so the unset-last sort rule cannot drift from the optional's semantics; the sort key surface is a plain Int (sortRank / ordinalValue with Int.max for unset) shared by one stable-ordering helper.

Deadline validation is constructive (failable inits are the only construction path), so the invalid-to-unset rule holds identically at every boundary: user input parse, model setter, and the lenient decode of a corrupt stored value.

Sort-tie stability is enforced by construction (enumerated + offset tie-break) instead of relying on the standard library sort, whose stability is undocumented; the spec makes stable ties a requirement, so it must not rest on an implementation accident.

The evidence the fix rests on is the pty's foreground process (xghostty_surface_foreground_pid = tcgetpgrp, plus proc_pidpath): while a pane is really remote, the local foreground process is ssh; back at its own prompt it is the pane's shell. The hard design point was NOT regressing the remote case: dropping the report on every OSC 133 D would have broken a remote bash session (its own re-report is suppressed for an unchanged PWD, so the pane would fall back to local after the first remote command). Hence the rule is conditional on the foreground: drop only when the pane's own shell is in front (that is the ssh-exit moment), keep otherwise. summary: T-064 (ledger inversion, model layer) completed and all three gates green (zig build / just test / just swift-test = exit 0, 590 Swift tests). The interrupted cycle R-20260818T031953 had landed WorkspaceState's ledger rework and ProjectLayoutType but left the tree uncompilable (ProjectListColumn missing, duplicate isProjectHidden, WorkspaceModel still assigning the now-private(set) canonicalProjectTree, SplitTree min/max shadowing). This cycle finished it: added ProjectListColumn (default order + normalizedOrder repair), rewrote projectListRows to the single unpartitioned ledger order, rewired every WorkspaceModel mutation onto ledger operations (insert below anchor, setProjectHidden for hide/show with rows keeping their positions, removeProject for close, row-swap for move_project, all-row applyProjectOrder for the sort actions), made project-boundary resize/equalize no-ops (abolition sanctioned by must-55; the Zig actions are removed in T-066), turned the old registered-layout application into a visible-row-reorder shim (T-065/T-066 replace it), updated the affected suites to the new semantics, and added ProjectLedgerTests covering T-064's four test requirements. Also fixed a real bug the interrupted cycle wrote: insertProject judged the visible cap AFTER inserting the row, so the 9th project wrongly arrived hidden.
decisions: Ledger semantics for show/close: a project returns to ITS OWN ledger row (no trailing-leaf re-attach); hidden rows are persisted facts, so restore no longer re-attaches orphans — tests rewritten accordingly.

Sort actions now reorder ALL rows (hidden included) via applyProjectOrder, since the visible-only state APIs were removed by the inversion; T-068 still owns its success-condition tests and the remaining guard refinements.

Kept the old layout selector / hide-selection machinery compiling as transitional shims routed through the ledger rather than deleting them mid-batch; their replacement is exactly T-065/T-066/T-067's scope.

summary: T-065 (layout types, success condition 15) completed; all three gates green (zig build / just test / just swift-test = exit 0, 603 Swift tests). The slot/choice/tree implementation had landed with T-064's state rework, so this cycle was verification work: 13 new ProjectLayoutTypeTests pin the distribution table for 1-9, wide slot geometry against an independent in-test computation of the definition, the tall=transpose-of-wide relationship (with row-/column-major swapping under transposition), pedestal composition (top rule x t/(t+1) split, bottom always last), the per-count exact-match-collapsed choice sets hand-derived independently (n=1: 1, n=2: 2, n=3: 5 with pedestal/row-major collapsing into wide/row-major, n=9: 4 with the tall progressions absorbed by the wide representatives), representative resolution, orientation-driven row assignment via hand-built SplitTree comparisons, ordinals following the list order rather than the visual position, and auto-apply of a remembered non-default type on every visible-count-changing operation with no re-forming on count-preserving ones (rename/priority/note/terminated transition). Everything passed first-run, so the T-064-era implementation matches the Essence definition without changes.
decisions: Derived the expected collapse sets by hand before writing the tests (notably: at n=9 the kept representatives are wide/rowMajor and wide/columnMajor, absorbing the tall progressions over the identical 3x3 grid — consistent with the Essence's '2 distinct progressions' example even though the labels differ from '横長型と縦長型').
Left the type-selection path (model API to set layoutType + the Cmd+Opt+L selector rework on choices(forVisibleCount:)) to T-066 as scoped; tests set layoutType via the state initializer.

summary: T-066 (layout-type selector rework + resize/equalize abolition) completed; all three gates green (zig build / just test / just swift-test = exit 0, 596 Swift tests). The Cmd+Opt+L selector now lists only the current visible count's exact-match-collapsed ProjectLayoutType choices (cursor seeded on the remembered type's representative, Enter applies via the new WorkspaceModel.chooseLayoutType - remember + relayout + close, never touching the project count or the ledger - Esc/backdrop cancel, and a single choice shows a nothing-to-choose message). The whole registered-layout machinery is gone: ProjectLayout.swift and its 16 tests deleted, chooseLayout/applyLayout/hide-pick and the transitional applyLayoutTree shim removed from the model, the shortfall/hide-pick UI blocks removed from TerminalWorkspaceView, and 9 new ProjectLayoutSelectionTests cover the surviving session. resize_project / equalize_projects are removed end to end (Zig action enum + parse tests + dispatch + palette + 5 default keybinds, both xghostty.h enum tags + union member, Swift dispatch/performability/notifications/observers/controller paths, the model no-ops) - a mid-enum C ABI removal done on both sides together and verified by checkXGhosttyHEnum. Project boundaries render through a new non-interactive FixedSplitView (no drag handle, no double-click), while zoomed pane dividers keep the interactive SplitView, satisfying success condition 16's resize clause.
decisions: Replaced SplitView with a local non-interactive FixedSplitView for project boundaries instead of adding a disable flag to the shared SplitView: the pane layer keeps its upstream-shaped interactive component untouched, and the project layer's fixed projection gets exactly zero interaction affordances.
Kept canBeginLayoutSelection permissive (opens even with a single choice) so the selector itself shows the nothing-to-choose message, per the Essence's success condition 16 wording.
SPEC.md sections 11.4/11.5/26 still describe the removed machinery in places; deferred the doc sweep to T-074 as scoped rather than doing a partial edit mid-batch.

summary: Context reset executed; counters zeroed.

The hide-selection screen is fully removed (WorkspaceModel session block ~120 lines, ProjectHideSelector view, controller/App/view wiring, 15 tests); the App action performability and the new controller hideFocusedProject() now route through canHideFocusedProject, which also refuses while the note editor or an overlay session owns the keyboard (new guard + new test). decisions: canHideFocusedProject subsumes the old canBeginHideSelection guard set (note editor / overlay sessions) so the immediate hide keeps the same keyboard-ownership discipline the selection screen had; the model method itself now refuses, keeping performability and mutation in agreement.

summary: T-068 done: sort layer finished per success condition 11. Renamed sortVisibleProjectsBy* -> sortProjectsBy* / canSortProjects (the actions sort all ledger rows including hidden; the old 'Visible' names misstated the scope). Resolved the open design point from the handoff: canSortProjects no longer refuses while the project list is open — S-046 says sorting works with or without the list open — but still refuses during the viewing-only note overview and the layout selector, whose listed choices must not be reshuffled underneath. Added tests: sorting with the list open keeps the session up and re-renders rows; post-sort ordinals skip a hidden row sorted to the ledger top (first visible row = ordinal 1). Existing coverage (all-row incl. hidden, stable ties, unset last, explicit-only persistence) confirmed sufficient. Gates: zig build 0 / just test 0 / just swift-test 0 (0 failures, 1 pre-existing skip). Next batch: T-069 (next trigger).
decisions: The project list is excluded from the sort refusal set while the note overview and layout selector remain in it: S-046's 'with or without the list open' is explicit for the list, and the list renders live state so a reorder under it is coherent; the other two overlays are viewing/choice sessions whose displayed order must stay stable.
